banner: SAMAY-DEMO-1 is SYNTHETIC: its rates are made up and are not UP tariff rates. This is not a real bill.

recommendations.title: Avoid the excess demand penalty
recommendations.finding: Maximum demand 337.125 kVA exceeded the contract demand of 300.000 kVA by 37.125 kVA, which triggers the excess demand charge (1.5x the demand rate).
recommendations.action: Stagger the start of large loads (compressors, furnaces, motors) so the 15-minute peak stays below contract demand, or review the contract demand with the utility if this peak is routine.
recommendations.confidence_reason: Both values are read from the bill; the excess is measured.

saving.note: Illustrative only: recalculated with SAMAY-DEMO-1, a SYNTHETIC tariff. This shows how the saving arises; it is not a real-world saving.

basis: Scenario: the same bill with recorded maximum demand equal to contract demand, recalculated with the same tariff.
Saving = current total - scenario total (includes demand, excess demand, duty and rounding).

recommendations.title: Raise power factor to cut billed kVAh
recommendations.finding: Average power factor is 0.917. Energy is billed on kVAh, so every unit of reactive power is paid for: 76333.333 kVAh were billed for 70010.000 kWh of useful energy.
recommendations.action: Install or repair automatic power factor correction (capacitor banks) near inductive loads to bring power factor to 0.99.
recommendations.confidence_reason: Power factor is calculated from the bill; reaching the target needs correctly sized capacitors.

saving.note: Illustrative only: recalculated with SAMAY-DEMO-1, a SYNTHETIC tariff. This shows how the saving arises; it is not a real-world saving.

basis: Scenario: the same kWh at power factor 0.99 (kVAh = kWh / 0.99, rounded up to 0.001), each zone scaled in proportion, recalculated with the same tariff.
assumptions: Power factor 0.99 is a common target for automatic correction; the capacitor cost is not included.

recommendations.title: Shift flexible load out of peak hours
recommendations.finding: 15266.667 kVAh (20.0% of the month) was used in peak hours (18:00-22:00), which cost 250.00 paise/kVAh more than off-peak (22:00-06:00).
recommendations.action: Move batch processes, water pumping, chilling or charging that can run at night into the off-peak window.
recommendations.confidence_reason: Zone readings are from the bill; how much load can move is an assumption.

saving.note: Illustrative only: recalculated with SAMAY-DEMO-1, a SYNTHETIC tariff. This shows how the saving arises; it is not a real-world saving.
saving.scenario: 1526.666 kVAh moved from peak to off-peak

basis: Scenario: 10% of peak energy (1526.666 kVAh) moved to off-peak, total energy unchanged, recalculated with the same tariff.
assumptions: 10% of peak-hour energy is assumed to be flexible. The bill does not show which loads run at peak.

recommendations.title: Peaky load profile
recommendations.finding: Load factor is 30.4%: average apparent load over the period compared with the maximum demand. A low load factor means short, high peaks relative to the average, which drive the demand charge.
recommendations.action: Spread high loads more evenly across shifts.
recommendations.confidence_reason: Uses monthly totals; interval data would show the peaks.

saving.note: Not priced: shown to explain the demand charge.

basis: Load factor = kVAh / (maximum demand kVA x hours in the period).

recommendations.finding: These lines were taken as printed, not recalculated: Meter rent ₹1,250.00.
recommendations.action: Check each against the tariff order and your agreement with the utility (for example meter rent for a meter you own).
recommendations.confidence_reason: The tariff rules for these lines are not modelled.
